subject: Post-call: Devkit sandbox & integration playbook for BrightPath
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@brightpath.health>, Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@brightpath.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Devkit sandbox & integration checklist

Alex / Natalie — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from the discovery and a concrete dev next-step list so your engineers can get a sandbox running this week.

High-level recap:
- Goal: embed semantic search + reranking into BrightPath clinical search and enable a structured output path to create tickets in your internal triage system.
- Preferred runtime: Node/TypeScript (Alex mentioned); Python is OK for ML pipelines but primary product work will be TS.
- Security: You require SOC 2 evidence and the option for VPC/private deployment; initial pilot should use hosted with strict logging and audit trails, then evaluate Dedicated if throughput needs rise.
- Data residency: US-only; we can pin region to us-west-2.

Immediate asks / next steps for engineering (assigned):
1) Run local devkit sandbox (Ben) — I attached a minimal devkit-readme.md with environment steps and example configs.
2) Provide sample payloads for your reranker + embeddings (BrightPath) — Natalie to share expected schema and sample documents.
3) Confirm auth method: API key for sandbox, OIDC/JWKS for production (Jonas will draft an OIDC integration note).
4) Identify one internal ticketing endpoint for structured tool-calling testing (Alex).

Attachments: devkit-readme.md (quick local steps), MAP-BRP-5421.pdf (mutual action plan draft).

Timing: If you can confirm the ticketing endpoint and share a small sample dataset by Monday 11/9, we can hand you a running sandbox by 11/12.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
Note: devkit-readme.md includes two sample configs (TS/Node and Python), guidance on env vars (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION) and a local mock server for structured output testing.

From: Alex Rivera <alex@brightpath.health>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Devkit sandbox & integration checklist

Thanks Ben — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: we want TypeScript-first sample app (Node 18). The data engineering team will run a Python ETL for embeddings but product teams want the SDK experience in TS.
- Reranker: we plan to use embeddings + a lightweight neural reranker. We'll share a 300-document sample and the ranking labels tomorrow.
- Ticketing: we use an internal API (ticketing@brightpath.health) that accepts JSON POSTs with a strict schema. We'll share the schema and a sandbox endpoint.
- Compliance: SOC 2 attestation and audit logs are mandatory for pilots with PHI. Can you confirm what is included in the MAP doc regarding audit logs?

Small ask: can the sandbox include a sample structured output/tool-calling flow that returns a verified JSON object (ticket_id, severity, notes) and a fallback free-text note if parsing fails? That will help our frontend team validate integration UX without hitting prod systems.

Appreciate the timeline — we aim to get samples to you by Monday.

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product, BrightPath Health

Subject: Re: Post-call: Devkit sandbox & integration checklist (technical notes)

Adding some technical detail for your engineers so they can spin up the sandbox quickly. I'll loop in a short checklist below and a config snippet.

Local sandbox checklist (Jonas):
- Clone: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devkit-samples
- Branch: use branch brp-5421/sandbox (contains TypeScript sample + Python ETL).
- Env vars (local .env): REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-..., REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2, REDWOOD_SANDBOX=true
- Start mock server: npm run start:mock (serves /tool/ticket endpoint to exercise structured output).
- Embeddings: python etl/embed_docs.py --input sample_docs.json --out embeddings.json (Python 3.10, venv recommended)

TypeScript sample (minimal):
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: process.env.REDWOOD_REGION });

// structured output example
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-instruct-1',
  prompt: 'Create ticket JSON from the following patient note:
---\n' + note,
  structured: { schema: { ticket_id: 'string', severity: 'string', notes: 'string' }, fallback: 'text_fallback' }
});

Notes on auth & routing:
- Sandbox: API key + allowlist on our side for the dev IPs.
- Prod: recommend OIDC with a short-lived token exchange (we provide a token introspection endpoint).
- Routing: set a policy to route low-latency calls (tool-calling / ticket creation) to a small dedicated pool to avoid queuing behind bulk embedding jobs. Our console can create a per-route policy.

I'll prepare a short OIDC integration example and drop it in the repo by EOD. Also attached: a short mapping file that maps your ticket schema to the SDK structured-output schema.

Jonas
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
